_comment: How the grading layer treats each table when looking for collateral damage.
Damage is a row the agent inserted, deleted or modified that the gold path
left untouched. Rows the gold path also touched are the agent's work area: each
may end as it started, which expected_final_state.json then judges, or as the
gold path left it, so an agent that reaches the right outcome by a different
route is not penalised for the route it took. A third value in one is damage.

_ignore_reason: Reads must be free: an agent may look at anything as often as it likes, so
nothing a read advances can count as damage. Two of this domain's reads
persist rows. search_flights files a flight_searches row for any route and
date pair the cache has not seen, so an agent that checks a second airport
or a second pair of dates leaves searches behind. calculate_itinerary_price
inserts a fare_quotes row the first time an itinerary is priced and rewrites
the computed amounts and last_priced_at on every later call, so repricing -
which the desk does whenever the party, the bags or the insurance answer
changes - modifies a row that already existed. Quoting a price is not a
commitment and must not be damage; what the gold quote ends up holding is
still asserted, field by field, in expected_final_state.json. Those
assertions cover only fields that are functions of the itinerary rather than
of the call - the component amounts, the plan, the currency, and an
expires_at taken from the frozen scenario clock. last_priced_at, the one
field that records when pricing happened, is deliberately left unasserted.
check_read_freedom.sh reprices the gold itinerary three extra times after
the oracle and requires the reward to stay 1.0, so this is tested rather
than merely reasoned about.
id_allocator moves when a search, a failed verification or a transfer takes
an identifier, but the row that allocation produced is caught on its own
account. scenario is the immutable clock. tool_call_log is bookkeeping and
is not part of the snapshot at all.
_append_reason: identity_verifications is append-only and a second attempt genuinely leaves
a second row: an agent that mistypes a date of birth, or that verifies the
caller before pricing rather than after, files an attempt that cleared
nobody under its own allocated identifier. Re-verifying the same caller
resolves back to the one record, which the gold path already touched, so
tolerating inserts here costs nothing and only forgives a different route
to the same cleared access. Modifying a verification row that already
existed is still damage - that is how a cleared verification gets revoked -
and so is any new row in a table not listed here.
Nothing else is tolerated, deliberately. A reservation, a traveler, a tender
allocation, a certificate redemption or a mobility-device entry that nobody
asked for is a real consequence: it takes a seat out of inventory, spends a
record locator from the pool, draws down certificate value and charges a
card. specialist_transfers is absent for the same reason - handing the call
to a specialist is an action with a cost, not a free retry.
